about: Control suite of tools/claims_check_r4.py. Items with a 'source' file name are copied verbatim (id, rule, expect, text, context) from that file under verification/audits/infrastructure/claims-check-redesign-20261125/work/, and their 'pinned' verdict is that directory's reference prototype work/proto.r4.py for the item's rule (verdict, codes) and over every rule (any). Categories: acceptance (the 195 preserved controls), probe (the review probes), heldout-W (batch W), diagnostic (author diagnostics D-01..D-12), example (the design example sentences EX-1..EX-6; 'expect' FAIL there marks a must-not-pass text, the source states its outcome in design terms), and previous-gap (the independent review of PR #1578: sentences that tools/claims_check.py flags, 'old_flags', and this checker passes, pinned as they are, a known and unresolved coverage gap). The self-test fails on any changed pinned verdict, and on a MISS or FPFAIL in the acceptance and probe categories. tools/claims_check_r4_test.py checks the copies against their sources, the pins of copied items against the prototype, and the old checker's verdict on the previous-gap items.

**Chandrasekaran, Longo, Penington and Witten [35]** showed that adding an observer to QFT in a de Sitter static patch promotes the von Neumann algebra of observables from type III to type II$_1$, with a well-defined trace and a renormalized entropy defined up to a state-independent additive constant; Witten [36] presents that algebra as the algebra of observables along the observer's worldline.
Witten's Type II algebra programme defines a renormalized entropy, finite for semiclassical states and fixed up to a state-independent additive constant, without finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.

Chandrasekaran, Longo, Penington, and Witten (CLPW) showed that the von Neumann algebra of QFT observables in a gravitational subregion promotes from type III to type II once an observer is included, with a renormalized entropy defined up to a state-independent additive constant. Harlow, Usatyuk, and Zhao established that the closed-universe Hilbert-space dimension is determined by the observer's degrees of freedom.

The construction gives the observer's operator algebra as a *Type II* von Neumann factor (rather than Type III, the algebra of operators in standard quantum field theory), with well-defined density matrices and a renormalized entropy defined up to a state-independent additive constant. The construction is observer-relative: different observers in de Sitter space have different algebras.

CLPW's entropy is the renormalized entropy of a Type II$_1$ algebra, defined up to a state-independent additive constant; it is not the ordinary von Neumann entropy of a finite-dimensional density matrix used in the framework.
